subject: Pedestrian segmentation at scale - relevant to .lumen's pipeline?
text:
Hi [NAME],

Came across .lumen's pedestrian segmentation work: building ADAS-grade
perception into a wearable is a serious data challenge, especially when
you're iterating on edge cases across 20+ countries of walking environments.

At Encord, we work with teams like Woven by Toyota and Skydio on exactly
this kind of perception pipeline: semantic segmentation, 3D scene
annotation, and video curation at scale. We recently published a deep-dive
on ADAS annotation pipelines
<[LINK]>
that
might be worth a read.

Worth 15 minutes to see if there's any overlap with where your team is at?

subject: Boston Dynamics' multimodal data management solution
text:
Hi [NAME],

We recently released EMM-1
<[LINK]>
-
the world's largest open-source multimodal dataset, with 107 million image,
video, text, audio and point cloud embeddings - and thought it might be
relevant given the vision and 3D data challenges behind HA-HA robotic
systems.

Our team has been building dataset curation and label tooling specifically
for visual AI teams at this stage of scale - we're working with teams like
Boston Dynamics and 1X, and would love to get your take on what we've
shipped.

Would you be open to a quick 15-minute chat to take a look, see if there's
any overlap, and share some honest feedback?

subject: Startup Innovation connection - Encord/[COMPANY]
text:
Hi [NAME],

Thanks for visiting our website - great to meet you.

I lead enterprise partnerships at Encord (YC company;100M series C), where
I work closely with innovation and technical teams supporting them to
explore how to move AI/ML use cases from idea to production.

A common challenge we see in large organisations is that multimodal data
(video, images, sensor data) is often siloed or difficult to operationalise
- which slows down promising AI initiatives. We support teams in
structuring and preparing this data to unlock use cases like computer
vision based automated inspection, anomaly detection, and robotics & more
<[LINK]>-
working with companies such as Boston Dynamics, AbbVie, or AXA.

I'd be really interested to hear what kinds of AI or data-driven
initiatives you're currently exploring at [COMPANY], and see if there's any
overlap where we could support.

Would you be open to connect with us next week?

text:

subject: perception work - data pipelines
text:
Hi [NAME],

Saw you're working on perception & growing your research team. We've
onboarded robotics teams (Walden, AnyBotics & a few SF based humanoid
companies) around similar stages when they're scaling up real-world data
collection - thought this would be a good time to connect?

For context we help improve scalability of their annotation pipelines -
e.g. having system to index, auto-annotate and QA perception data across 2D
(image & video) and 3D point cloud/ LiDAR data in one place. With the goal
of accelerating their model iteration cycles & increasing labelling
throughput.

How are you thinking of your data requirements for the real world? I'm
flexible morning times EST if you're open to exchange perspectives.
